anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-layer statements or transaction boundaries are written in a way that forces the engine to touch more data, rows, or time than business logic requires.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions request mutually incompatible locks on the same resource, causing queues, blocking chains, or deadlocks in the lock manager.

When both root causes are present, the oversized or poorly filtered statements produced by the SQL Workload Logic Anomaly inflate the number of rows scanned, updated, or held open in a transaction. This broad lock footprint collides with other concurrent transactions, leading to prolonged blocking chains, frequent deadlocks, rising lock-wait times, and sharply deteriorating throughput. Symptoms include the same slow or long-running statements repeatedly appearing in both slow-query and lock-diagnostic logs, lock-wait metrics climbing in parallel with query execution time, application timeouts that coincide with deadlock victim rollbacks, and connection pools backing up even when hardware resources are not saturated.

Causally, inefficient workload logic extends transaction duration and expands the set of locked resources, thereby amplifying the probability and severity of lock contention. In turn, lock waits stall the inflated statements even longer, further lengthening transaction lifetimes and broadening their lock scopes. This positive feedback loop magnifies performance degradation, makes individual root causes harder to isolate, and can push the database into a persistent low-throughput, high-latency state until either the workload logic is corrected or lock pressure is relieved.

entry.official_definition: The length of time in seconds an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock before giving up.
entry.trigger_condition: An InnoDB transaction waits longer than innodb_lock_wait_timeout for a row lock.
entry.workload_impact: The lock wait gives up; by default only the current statement is rolled back unless innodb_rollback_on_timeout is enabled.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as an InnoDB system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
